# TABLE PURPOSE INDEX — every object, what it is FOR, and the control that exposes it

**GENERATED by `scripts/build_table_purpose_index.py`. Do not hand-edit — regenerate.**

> Operator, 2026-08-19: *"index and understand every single table that is either used or
> derived within this application, and how it fits into our objectives."*

This answers the question the other three documents do not. `TABLE_INVENTORY.md` says what an
object CARRIES; `FEATURE_INVENTORY.md` maps features→tables and so cannot see a table that
reaches no feature; and the wiring census counts a *surface*, which includes a provenance line
nobody can click. **The question here is whether a USER CAN OPERATE A CONTROL that reaches it** —
which is the denominator for **G65** (every map feature its own toggle) and **G67** (the screener
filters on everything).

## The verdicts

| verdict | meaning | n |
|---|---|---:|
| **TOGGLE** | a checkbox or layer control the user can operate reaches it | **43** |
| **PAGE ONLY** | it reaches a filterable page, but no control names it — a G67 candidate | **78** |
| **READ-ONLY** | rendered, but nothing the user can ask a question with | **157** |
| **NO SURFACE** | reaches nothing at all | **20** |
| **INFRASTRUCTURE** | registries, censuses and join views — correctly not a control | **12** |

**310 objects.** ⭐ **43 of them can be turned on and off by the reader.**
Everything in PAGE ONLY and READ-ONLY is data we hold and the user cannot ask about.

## By objective

| objective | the developer question it answers | objects |
|---|---|---:|
| **P1 owner motivation** | who might sell, and how strongly we believe it | 74 |
| **P2 power & grid** | can I get power here, in the direction I need, and when | 64 |
| **P4 environmental** | what could stop or slow the permit | 39 |
| **P5 community & rules** | will the county let me build, and what have they done before | 36 |
| **P6 market & cost** | what will power actually cost me here | 35 |
| **context** | who else is here, and what does the local economy look like | 23 |
| **P3 land & size** | is there enough usable land, and how far to what matters | 22 |
| **infrastructure** | machinery: registries, censuses and join views | 16 |
| **unclassified** | — | 1 |

⚠ The objective classification is a **stated rule table** at the top of the generator, not a
judgement buried in prose. If a row is filed wrongly, fix the rule and regenerate — do not
edit this file.

## ⚠ Two limits of this instrument, stated rather than discovered later

**1. The control column resolves to PAYLOAD granularity, not layer granularity.** Several
controls draw from one payload — `L-bus`, `L-lines` and `L-subs` all read `grid.geojson.gz` —
so a table feeding only the bus half is credited to all three. The verdict (is there ANY control)
is sound; treat the named controls as *the controls on the payload it feeds*.

**2. Table→payload is proximity-scoped, not parsed.** ⛔ The first version cross-produced every
table a script mentions with every payload it writes, and claimed `in_sites` — the 3.55M-parcel
spine — was exposed by `L-terr`, the utility-territory checkbox. It now attributes a payload only
to tables named within ~2,500 characters of the write. That is an approximation and it will
mis-file some rows; it no longer invents whole categories of them.
